claims.text: Earlier work produced HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure containing multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Vacuum arc melting followed by a tailored thermomechanical treatment produces the stated hierarchical heterostructure in HfNbTiVAl10.
Convolutional neural networks can extract the size, distribution, and intensity of chemical fluctuations from high-resolution electron-microscopy images.
The extracted imaging descriptors can be fused with physics-based constraints in a model trained on a limited set of mechanically tested samples.
The proposed model can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Hierarchical chemical fluctuations and heterostructural features control local deformation and crack initiation.
The hierarchical distribution of chemical heterogeneities contains microstructural information relevant to elasticity, plastic onset, and fracture.
Embedding imaging-derived microstructural information in a physics-informed model can provide a surrogate for computationally expensive multiscale simulations.
Learning representative microstructural features reduces computational cost.
The integrated method will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 15% relative to CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, or standard machine learning used in isolation.
The integrated method will reduce computational time by approximately 100-fold relative to the stated conventional methods.
The method will reliably capture both bulk elastic-plastic properties and critical fracture behavior.
The stated predictions apply to room-temperature, quasi-static tensile testing in air at an approximate strain rate of 0.001 s^-1 and to fracture testing of precracked specimens.
Processing or environmental changes that substantially alter the heterostructure relative to the training data can make the method unreliable.
Insufficient imaging resolution can make the method unreliable when critical microstructural features are not resolved.
Failure to sample rare defects that strongly influence toughness can reduce model reliability.
Performance is uncertain for microstructures that deviate considerably from the model's training distribution.
